holidays.name: Phileas Fogg Wager Day
holidays.description: Pack a bag, check your watch and toast the world's most famous bet. This day honors the gentleman who wagered he could circle the globe in just 80 days.
holidays.origin: In Jules Verne's 1872 novel Around the World in Eighty Days, the proper Englishman Phileas Fogg makes his wager at the Reform Club on October 2. Fans mark the date as the starting point of his fictional journey.
holidays.funFact: Fogg has to finish by 8:45 p.m. on December 21. He nearly loses the bet, then wins it thanks to a crossing of the International Date Line that he hadn't realized gained him a day.

holidays.name: National Name Your Car Day
holidays.description: Time to give your trusty ride the identity it deserves. Whether it's a Lightning McBeast or a humble Gerald, today is for christening your car.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial, fun observance of unclear origin. It celebrates the very human habit of treating vehicles like members of the family.
holidays.funFact: Surveys of drivers have repeatedly found that a sizable share of people give their cars nicknames. Many say the car has a distinct personality.

holidays.name: Card Making Day
holidays.description: A day for scissors, glitter, stamps and glue. Crafters are encouraged to make a handmade card for someone, whether or not there's an occasion.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial craft observance of unclear origin. It encourages people to swap store-bought greetings for personal handmade ones.
holidays.funFact: Handmade greeting cards go back centuries. Early valentines were often hand-drawn and decorated with paper lace.
